title: The Atmosphere The Wise Services Of Clouds Wind Rain Lightning And Thunder

questions.question: Who is being spoken to in this part of the passage?
questions.answer: A traveler who is a guest in the world.

questions.question: What does the atmosphere tell the traveler to do?
questions.answer: It tells him to look carefully so he can find the One he is seeking.

questions.question: How is the atmosphere described at first?
questions.answer: It seems harsh in one way, but also gentle and helpful.

questions.question: What important job do the clouds do for the earth?
questions.answer: They bring water to the world.

questions.question: How do the clouds help living things besides bringing rain?
questions.answer: They make the weather less harsh and hurry to help where help is needed.

questions.question: What example shows that the clouds act in an organized way?
questions.answer: They appear and disappear like a trained army following orders.

questions.question: How quickly do the clouds gather when it is time for rain?
questions.answer: Very fast, within a short time.

questions.question: What does the traveler notice about the wind?
questions.answer: It is busy doing many useful jobs in a wise way.

questions.question: Name one thing the air helps carry to living things.
questions.answer: It carries heat, light, electricity, or sound.

questions.question: How does the air help plants?
questions.answer: It helps them get pollinated.

questions.question: Why is rain called “mercy” in this passage?
questions.answer: Because it brings many caring gifts and benefits from Allah.

questions.question: What are the raindrops like?
questions.answer: They are delicate, bright, and sweet.

questions.question: What two things does the traveler notice after looking at the rain?
questions.answer: Lightning and thunder.

questions.question: Where does the traveler look in this passage?
questions.answer: He looks at the atmosphere, or the space above the earth.

questions.question: What does the atmosphere seem to say to him?
questions.answer: It says that he can learn through it about the One who sent him.

questions.question: What sound in the atmosphere catches the traveler’s attention?
questions.answer: Thunder.

questions.question: Between what two places are the clouds hanging?
questions.answer: Between the sky and the earth.

questions.question: What do the clouds give to the people and creatures of the earth?
questions.answer: Water needed for life.

questions.question: What does the passage show about the clouds when they cannot be seen?
questions.answer: They can go away completely for a time, as if waiting for orders.

questions.question: When the order for rain comes, what do the clouds do?
questions.answer: They gather quickly and fill the sky.

questions.question: What does the traveler learn from the many jobs of the air?
questions.answer: It is working in an orderly and generous way.

questions.question: How does the air help both animals and people?
questions.answer: It gives them breath and carries sound.

questions.question: What does the air bring to living things besides breath?
questions.answer: It brings warmth, light, and electricity.

questions.question: What does the traveler understand about the drops of rain?
questions.answer: They carry many gifts and helpful purposes.

questions.question: What does the rain seem to show in a visible way?
questions.answer: Allah’s mercy.

questions.question: Which two weather events are said to have special jobs too?
questions.answer: Lightning and thunder.

questions.question: Who is welcomed as a guest in the world in this passage?
questions.answer: The traveler.

questions.question: What part of creation begins speaking to the traveler here?
questions.answer: The atmosphere.

questions.question: What is the traveler searching for through these signs?
questions.answer: The One who made him and sent him.

questions.question: What does the passage say the clouds do for the world like a garden?
questions.answer: They water it.

questions.question: How do the clouds show mercy to the earth’s creatures?
questions.answer: They bring life-giving water and help when it is needed.

questions.question: What comparison is used for the clouds when they appear and disappear?
questions.answer: A disciplined army.

questions.question: What does this comparison teach about the clouds?
questions.answer: They act with order and obedience, not randomly.

questions.question: What does the traveler see when he studies the wind?
questions.answer: That it is used for many wise and useful tasks.

questions.question: How is sound connected to the work of the air?
questions.answer: The air carries it from place to place.

questions.question: What does the traveler see inside the raindrops, in a meaning sense?
questions.answer: Many gifts, benefits, and kindness.

questions.question: Why does the passage connect rain with mercy?
questions.answer: Because it comes with care and helps life.

questions.question: What does the traveler do after looking at rain?
questions.answer: He looks at lightning and listens to thunder.

questions.question: What place is called a wondrous gathering place in this passage?
questions.answer: The atmosphere, or the space above us.

questions.question: What invitation does this place give the traveler?
questions.answer: To look at it and learn from it.

questions.question: What mixed look does the atmosphere have?
questions.answer: It looks a little stern, yet also kind.

questions.question: What weather event is described as loud but happy in a way?
questions.answer: Thunder.

questions.question: What do the clouds provide for the earth?
questions.answer: Water for life.

questions.question: How do the clouds help with heat?
questions.answer: They make the natural heat softer and more balanced.

questions.question: What tells us the clouds are under command?
questions.answer: They can vanish and then come back quickly when needed.

questions.question: How fast can the clouds come together for rain?
questions.answer: In a very short time.

questions.question: What does the passage say about the number of jobs the air does?
questions.answer: It does many, many jobs.

questions.question: Give one job of the air that is not breathing.
questions.answer: Carrying sound, bringing light, bringing heat, bringing electricity, or helping plants.

questions.question: How are the raindrops described in a gentle way?
questions.answer: They are soft-looking, shining, and sweet.

questions.question: What hidden source do the raindrops seem to come from?
questions.answer: A treasure of mercy.

questions.question: Why is it fitting that rain is called “mercy”?
questions.answer: Because it brings caring help and blessings.

questions.question: In this passage, what part of the world seems to speak first?
questions.answer: The atmosphere.

questions.question: What does it promise the traveler he can do through it?
questions.answer: He can find the One he is looking for.

questions.question: What do the clouds do to the earth that makes it like a watered garden?
questions.answer: They send down water.

questions.question: Who benefits from the water of the clouds?
questions.answer: The dwellers of the earth, meaning living things on earth.

questions.question: What else do the clouds fix besides dryness?
questions.answer: They help balance heat.

questions.question: What picture helps us understand the clouds’ obedience?
questions.answer: Soldiers in a well-trained army.

questions.question: What happens right after the order to send rain?
questions.answer: The clouds gather very quickly.

questions.question: What does the wind show about how the air is used?
questions.answer: It is used wisely, generously, and in an orderly way.

questions.question: Why is it amazing that the air does so many jobs?
questions.answer: Because it seems lifeless, yet it serves many needs so well.

questions.question: What are some needs the air helps meet for living things?
questions.answer: Breathing, warmth, light, electricity, sound, and plant pollination.

questions.question: What does the traveler notice inside the rain in addition to water?
questions.answer: Many acts of kindness and help.

questions.question: What name is given to rain because of these blessings?
questions.answer: Mercy.

questions.question: What two final signs in the sky does the traveler observe here?
questions.answer: Lightning and thunder.

questions.question: Who is learning from the signs in this passage?
questions.answer: A traveler in the world.

questions.question: What does the atmosphere want the traveler to understand?
questions.answer: That it can guide him to the One who sent him.

questions.question: Which part of the atmosphere’s face does the traveler notice?
questions.answer: It seems rough, yet caring.

questions.question: What weather sound helps him notice the atmosphere’s message?
questions.answer: Thunderclaps.

questions.question: What do the clouds do in a wise and caring way?
questions.answer: They water the earth and help life.

questions.question: How do the clouds show they are ready to serve?
questions.answer: They go where help is needed and gather quickly when called.

questions.question: What does the clouds’ fast gathering teach us?
questions.answer: That they work under command and order.

questions.question: What does the traveler learn by looking at the wind?
questions.answer: The air is busy with many planned jobs.

questions.question: What does the air carry to living things?
questions.answer: Breath, heat, light, electricity, and sound.

questions.question: How does the air help plants make seeds and grow?
questions.answer: It helps move pollen.

questions.question: What makes the raindrops special in the traveler’s eyes?
questions.answer: They are full of gentle gifts and benefits.

questions.question: If rain is called mercy, what does that tell us about it?
questions.answer: It is a caring gift, not just plain water.

questions.question: After rain, what two signs does the traveler pay attention to?
questions.answer: Lightning and thunder.
